# grill-me - interrogate before you build

GRILL -> SPEC -> PLAN -> BUILD -> TEST -> VERIFY -> HANDOFF, not IDEA -> BUILD
(GENESIS.md "The sequence"). This skill is the GRILL step. It exists because
this estate measured seven things proposed in one week that already existed,
and because the fastest way to ship the wrong thing is to start typing before
the ambiguity is gone.

## SOURCE FILE - read this before copying anything

This file has ONE body, committed at `claude/skills/grill-me/SKILL.md` in the
`zaal-dotfiles` repo. Every other path that can run it is a symlink or a
render pointing back here:

- Claude Code sees it because `claude/skills` is already a whole-directory
  symlink into `~/.claude/skills` (bootstrap.sh) - no extra step.
- Codex and Hermes Agent read `~/.agents/skills/grill-me/SKILL.md`, a symlink
  into this repo file (same direction bootstrap.sh already uses everywhere

- Antigravity reads `.agents/workflows/grill-me.md` per repo. Rendering that
  symlink into every Antigravity-enabled repo is a SEPARATE task (plan 5,
  agentic-infrastructure-plan-2026-09-10-5-antigravity.md). Do not hand-copy
  this file into an `.agents/workflows/` directory - wait for that renderer,

  others are not.

If you are editing the checklist, the close, or the ZAO-specific sections
below, edit THIS file and nowhere else.

## When to fire

- Someone types `/grill-me`, or says "grill me on this", "interrogate this
  idea", "help me spec this", "spec this out", or hands over something that
  sounds like a new capability, a new bot, a new automation, or a change to
  something several lanes depend on.
- Any time you (the agent) are about to propose a design and realize you do
  not actually know the outcome, the constraints, or what must not change.
- NOT for clearing a backlog of already-scoped decisions - that is
  `quick-grill` (see "grill-me vs quick-grill" below). Do not run both on the
  same ask.

## Step zero: MEASURE before you ask a single question

Before the checklist, before any question, read what already exists:

- `SYSTEM_MAP.md` - what is already built and running.
- `DECISIONS.md` (and the `decisions/` files it indexes) - what is already
  decided, so you do not re-litigate it.

A question whose answer is already sitting in the vault is a wasted tap. Name
the closest existing thing before proposing to build anything, even when the
honest answer is "nothing close exists" - say that too, out loud, so it is on
the record rather than assumed.

## The checklist (Brandon, spec 7.1) - work through every item, out loud

1. **What outcome, exactly?** Not the feature - the outcome. What does the
   world look like once this exists that it does not look like now?
2. **Who is it for?** The principal directly, a lane, a bot, an external
   user. A different answer changes the whole design.
3. **What existing systems does this touch or duplicate?** This is where
   step zero's measurement pays off - name the closest existing thing.
4. **Constraints.** Time, machine, budget, who has to approve it, anything
   already decided in `DECISIONS.md` that bounds the answer.
5. **Dependencies.** What has to exist first. What this blocks once it ships.
6. **What must NOT change.** The invariant a good implementation is not
   allowed to break, stated positively, not as a vague "don't break anything."
7. **Permissions required.** What authority does executing this require, and
   which door is it - GENESIS.md's "Authority" section names the two-way and
   one-way doors and the escalation classes; this skill does not restate
   them, it just asks which one applies.
8. **Success criteria.** Stated as something that can be measured after the
   fact, not as a feeling.
9. **Failure conditions.** What does "this did not work" look like, concretely
   enough that a session six weeks from now can tell the difference between
   failed and merely unfinished.
10. **Smallest useful version.** What is the least that is still worth
    shipping, before any of the nice-to-haves.

**Challenge assumptions.** After the checklist, restate the request back with
every assumption made explicit, and ask whether each one is actually true.
This is where most bad specs get caught - not in the checklist itself, but in
the restatement. Say plainly what has not been considered yet, rather than
letting a gap stay quietly unmentioned.

## The close - stop here, every time

When ambiguity is sufficiently reduced, produce, in this order, and then STOP:

1. **Specification summary** - the outcome, the constraints, the success and
   failure criteria, in one tight paragraph plus the smallest useful version.
2. **Proposed architecture** - the shape of the solution, not the code.
3. **Affected systems** - every file, script, hook, cron line or lane brief
   this will touch, named, not implied.
4. **Implementation plan** - ordered, with real files and real commands where
   already known (hand off to `superpowers:writing-plans` when the ask is big
   enough to warrant a separate plan document).
5. **Approval before consequential execution.** A two-way door can proceed
   once the above is written down. A one-way door (GENESIS.md "Authority")
   always waits for an explicit answer, tap or text, before anything
   irreversible runs.

Do not fold step 5 into step 4. The plan is not the approval.

## ZAO-specific outputs - what makes this worth more than a generic grill

- **The output is a spec file, not code.** Write it to `zao-vault/projects/`
  (the same location every other ZAO spec lives - see the files already
  there for naming: `<topic>-YYYY-MM-DD.md` or, for a numbered plan,
  `agentic-infrastructure-plan-YYYY-MM-DD-<n>-<slug>.md`).
- **The handoff is `superpowers:writing-plans`**, not an implementation skill.
  grill-me's job ends at the written spec and the stop-for-approval gate;
  writing-plans turns an approved spec into an implementation plan.
- **Gates are named by reference, not copied.** This file points at
  GENESIS.md "Authority" and "The sequence" rather than restating their
  wording, so the two documents cannot drift apart. If the gate you need
  is not clearly covered there, that is a gap in GENESIS.md to raise, not a
  license to invent a new rule here.
- **End every grill by writing down what was decided, durably, in two
  places:**
  1. The spec file in `zao-vault/projects/` - the specification itself.
  2. A `decisions/<slug>.md` file (matching the frontmatter shape used by
     every other file in `zao-vault/decisions/`: `type: decision`, `date`,
     `tags: [decision]`, `status`) for anything decided during the grill that
     would otherwise get re-litigated later - a rejected alternative, a
     constraint someone stated once and will forget, a "we are not doing X."
     `DECISIONS.md` itself is generated (`scripts/build-decisions-index.py`);
     never hand-edit it, only add the decision file and regenerate.

## Ask in batches, tap not type

Wherever the checklist above produces a multiple-choice or multi-pick
question, ask it with AskUserQuestion in batches of at most four, recommended
option first with a one-line why, and `multiSelect: true` whenever the
options are not mutually exclusive. The principal clears decisions by tapping,
not typing. This is exactly the batching pattern `quick-grill` uses - see
that skill for the mechanics; it is not repeated here. Save open text for the
items a checklist truly cannot turn into options (item 1, the outcome, almost
always needs a sentence, not a tap).

## In Claude Code: wrap superpowers:brainstorming, do not duplicate it

When this skill runs inside Claude Code, invoke the Skill tool with
`skill: "superpowers:brainstorming"` first. Its three paths (spike, bounded,
architectural), its hard approval gate, and its terminal states are all
correct and already enforced - this skill does not re-implement any of that.
grill-me adds Brandon's interrogation checklist on the front (step zero plus
the ten-item checklist above, run before or alongside brainstorming's own
questions) and the ZAO-specific outputs on the back (spec file location,
decisions/ file, gates named by reference instead of copied). Classify the
path exactly as brainstorming does, and let its ratchet rule stand: hidden
complexity discovered mid-grill upgrades the path, never downgrades it.

## In Codex, Hermes Agent and Antigravity

No AskUserQuestion tool and no `superpowers:brainstorming` skill exist there.
Run the same step zero, the same ten-item checklist, and the same close as
ordinary interrogation in the conversation - one or two questions per turn,
not a wall of ten at once - and still restate assumptions before closing, and
still write the spec file and any decisions/ file before stopping.

## grill-me vs quick-grill - say plainly which one to use

**grill-me (this skill)** is for a NEW, ambiguous ask, before anything
consequential is built: measures the vault first, interrogates until the
ambiguity is gone, ends in a specification file and a plan, and stops for
approval. Slow on purpose. Use it once per idea, at the start.

**quick-grill** (`claude/skills/quick-grill/SKILL.md`) is for clearing a
BACKLOG of decisions that are already scoped - questions that already have a
short list of options, not questions that still need a specification
written. Fast on purpose, tap-only, no architecture or plan produced. Use it
to clear pending calls, open a session, or walk through what an overnight
loop shipped. grill-me points at quick-grill for the batching mechanics
rather than restating them; do not copy quick-grill's guidance into this
file.

If unsure which applies: if the honest answer to "do I know the options
already" is no, it is grill-me. If the options already exist and the only
thing missing is a pick, it is quick-grill. Do not run both on the same ask.
